question: May approval prompts use a shortened preview only when every affected Control UI and native-channel surface provides an explicit way to inspect the complete sanitized command before Allow once or Allow always?
rationale: This is a product security boundary: readability improvements are useful, but hiding executable content changes what an operator can verify before granting authority.

options.title: Require full-command inspection
options.body: Keep a compact preview if needed, but add an explicit full-command reveal, scroll, or copy path before any approval action across all affected presentation surfaces.

options.title: Accept preview-only approvals
options.body: Intentionally allow operators to approve unseen command tails in exchange for shorter prompts, with the resulting security tradeoff documented.

options.title: Limit this PR to decision rendering
options.body: Drop the command-summary changes and retain only a rebased Control UI implementation of gateway-provided allowed decisions.

recommendation.title: Require full-command inspection
recommendation.body: Keep a compact preview if needed, but add an explicit full-command reveal, scroll, or copy path before any approval action across all affected presentation surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most closely connects this contributor to the approval planner, allow-always, and approval-display boundary.
